situation.name: facebook_adoption_sir
situation.description: Traditional SIR model applied to Facebook adoption dynamics. Susceptible users become infected (join Facebook) through contact with current users, and recover (leave Facebook) at a constant rate.

article.name: Epidemiological modeling of online social network dynamics
article.author: Cannarella, J., Spechler, J.A.

data.name: facebook_google_trends_data
data.place: Google search query data for Facebook (Jan 2004 - Jul 2013)

params.name: infection_rate
params.meaning: Rate at which potential users join OSN through contact (1/time)

situation.name: facebook_adoption_irSIR
situation.description: Infectious recovery SIR (irSIR) model for Facebook. Recovery (abandonment) spreads infectiously - users leave when their peers leave. Requires contact between recovered and infected for recovery.

article.name: Epidemiological modeling of online social network dynamics
article.author: Cannarella, J., Spechler, J.A.

data.name: facebook_google_trends_data
data.place: Google search query data for Facebook (Jan 2004 - Jul 2013)

params.name: infection_rate
params.meaning: Rate at which potential users join OSN through contact (1/time)

params.name: infectious_recovery_rate
params.meaning: Infectious recovery rate - abandonment spreads through contact with recovered (1/time)

params.name: basic_reproductive_number
params.meaning: R0 = beta/gamma for SIR; for irSIR depends on R0 and nu

params.name: immunization_criterion
params.meaning: Condition for disease-free equilibrium stability in SIR
